content: The Houston Food Bank is recognized as the fifth largest food bank in the United States and is a member of America’s Second Harvest. Established in 1982, it operates as a private, non-profit organization with a mission to address hunger and food insecurity. The organization supplies food to over 400 non-profit hunger-relief agencies across southeast Texas. Within its 18-county service area, the Houston Food Bank supports a range of programs, including food pantries, shelters for the homeless, safe havens for survivors of domestic violence, and nutrition centers for children and the elderly. Each week, the Houston Food Bank provides nutritious food to approximately 80,000 individuals. Beyond food distribution, it offers nutrition education programs to the local community. These programs, such as Backpack Buddy, Community Kitchen, Kids Cafe, and Operation Frontline, are designed to equip participants with the knowledge and skills necessary to make informed, healthy food choices. In 2005, the Houston Food Bank distributed over 38 million pounds of food, which equates to approximately 63,000 meals per day. It serves as a critical food resource for numerous partner agencies and their clients, acting as a safety net against hunger and food insecurity for the Houston metropolitan area. Following Hurricane Katrina, the Houston Food Bank significantly increased its distribution efforts, more than doubling its standard rate of food and personal hygiene product distribution. Over a six-month period, it provided 7.8 million pounds of disaster relief items to local agencies assisting hurricane survivors. Despite its extensive operations, the organization maintains efficiency, with only 7% of its costs allocated to operational expenses.
